name: Synosseum-C
description: Synosseum-C is a hydroxyapatite-zirconia ceramic composite in which a network of viable osteocyte-analog cells is maintained within sealed lacunae distributed through the material matrix, connected by canalicular microchannels that allow nutrient and signal flow. Unlike passive bone-substitute ceramics, Synosseum-C actively participates in the local bone remodeling cycle — it resorbs and re-deposits material in response to mechanical load signals exactly as natural bone does, preventing the stress-shielding failures that plagued earlier-generation implants. It is the first ceramic implant material that genuinely co-evolves with the host skeleton.
cost: Φ6,500 per 100cc volume unit; custom anatomical pre-forms Φ15,000–Φ45,000
story_hooks: A patient implanted with Synosseum-C during a childhood injury is now an adult — and the ceramic has remodeled so completely over twenty years that it has changed shape, migrating subtly with skeletal growth in ways the original surgeons did not predict, now pressing against a nerve bundle.

A black-market surgeon is using Synosseum-C to conceal contraband inside bodies — items packed in the ceramic matrix will not appear on standard scans, and the material will grow into the surrounding bone, making retrieval nearly impossible without major surgery.

A Synosseum-C lot is contaminated with a rogue osteoclast-activating protein — recipients' implants are slowly resorbing at an accelerated rate, and the manufacturer is suppressing the data because a recall would bankrupt the division.
